title: Introduction to Networking
description: Fragmentation, MTU, and trade-offs in network design.
objectives: Explain why IP fragments need to be reassembled.
Distinguish PMTUD from PLPMTUD.
Analyse load balancing and packet ordering.

title: Networking Principles
description: Layering, addressing, the end-to-end principle, and multipath networking.
objectives: Distinguish PDUs, SDUs, and functions with different scopes.
Explain NAT, mobility, and MPTCP.
Evaluate end-to-end design and protocol extensions.

title: The Internet Transport Layer
description: TCP, UDP, acknowledgements, and loss recovery.
objectives: Interpret TCP sequence numbers, ACKs, and windows.
Analyse retransmissions and RTT measurements.
Compare loss recovery mechanisms and their impact on short flows.

title: Congestion Control
description: Windows, queues, congestion, and fair bandwidth allocation.
objectives: Calculate window sizes, bandwidth–delay products, and bandwidth shares.
Distinguish flow control from congestion control.
Evaluate RED, CoDel, ECN, BBR, and pacing.

title: Wireless Communications I
description: Radio waves, modulation, multiplexing, and MIMO.
objectives: Calculate wavelength, symbol rate, and channel capacity.
Distinguish TDMA, FDMA, CDMA, and OFDMA.
Explain MIMO, beamforming, and errors on wireless links.

title: Wireless Communications II
objectives: Analyse hidden terminals and RTS/CTS.
Distinguish the LTE control plane from the data plane.
Explain roaming and mobile virtual network operators.

title: Wireless Communications III
description: Massive IoT, LPWAN, LoRaWAN, and NB-IoT.
objectives: Compare LoRaWAN and NB-IoT in terms of coverage, spectrum, and infrastructure.
Explain how spreading factor and ADR affect airtime and link quality.
Evaluate trade-offs between coverage, energy use, and receive latency in NB-IoT.
